analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/reference/configuration.md (head lines ~923-1015, 1077-1104 plus date bumps). It documents that a signed release can register a `cluster_runtime` block (digests, pair_serving_grant, parity_qualifications) via POST /v1/releases, from which the coordinator derives cluster approvals, grants and qualifications. It also declares GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-27B publicly qualified in pipeline and tensor-parallel modes. No code, controls, endpoints or deployment settings change in the supplied evidence, so I found no concrete regression.

Points for the next pass:
(1) Lines 983-1002 state that public traffic is admitted on any Apple silicon pair, within the request envelope, even though no pipeline of either model ran on two M5 Ultras and GLM tensor parallel has no cross-cable record. This is an owner decision resting on weaker evidence. It touches the T-056/T-054 concern of overclaiming correctness. It is a policy statement in the docs, not a control regression.
(2) Release-registration authority (A-005, A-011, A-017) now also carries cluster approvals and qualifications through POST /v1/releases. The platform-owned coordinator must authenticate this and bind it to the release identity. That is outside the supplied evidence, so it is recorded as an unverified contract.
(3) Lines 1181-1182 say model approvals (no build pinning) are accepted only in DevNet. Production gating is coordinator-side and unverified here.
(4) The member-side checks (lines 1096-1104, digest comparison, HTTPS-only fetch, no redirect, bounded size, 404 means no approval) are documented as unchanged in kind.

No changed threat-model assumption is demonstrated. Whether TB-011 and T-054/T-055 need an update to mention the release-derived approvals and the public declaration is a documentation question for the owner.
